new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress falls on the first vowel that follows a consonant, i.e. the first syllable with an onset: the second surface syllable in the (predominant) vowel-initial words, the first in consonant-initial words; under Breen's VC(C) syllabification this is uniformly the second underlying syllable. Breen states this as the Arandic-wide rule and his own Western Anmatyerr notes (p.63) presuppose it (an initial vowel is unstressed, a vowel after an initial /y/ is stressed). Concurring: Koch 1997 p.286 'Stress in Arandic is on the first syllable beginning with a consonant (i.e. (V)'CV)'; Koch 2014 p.320 'in Arandic language stress is usually on the first syllable with an onset, which usually means the second syllable of the word', with Anmatyerr as the main data source.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not stated by Breen 2001. Koch 2014 p.321 refers to Arandic syllables 'with primary and secondary stress respectively' (second and third syllables of a Warlpiri loan) without giving a rule; for the sister variety Western Arrernte, Anderson 2000 p.41 (held by the project under west2441) gives secondary stress on every other following syllable except the final.
new_statements.exceptions: Breen 2001 (approx. pp.50-53, before the p.55 statement) notes that most speakers stress the initial rounded vowel of short words and that stress is transferred to the initial vowel in short surface VCV words; Western Anmatyerr often drops initial vowels altogether (p.64), so surface words become consonant-initial with initial stress. No Anmatyerr-specific lexical exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms. The statement is explicitly Arandic-wide (Arrernte varieties, Anmatyerr, Alyawarr, Kaytetye), from a linguist with first-hand fieldwork on Western Anmatyerr (Mt Allan, Napperby, Ti Tree) reported in the same paper; no Anmatyerr-only stress statement was opened (Green 2010 dictionary not seen).
new_statements.identity_note: anma1239 covers both Eastern/Central Anmatyerr (Ti Tree, Utopia; Green 2010) and Western Anmatyerr (Mt Allan, Napperby, Coniston; Breen 2001 sec. 4.7). Breen 2001's rule is stated for Arandic as a whole and applied by him to Western Anmatyerr; no separate glottocode for the western variety. Koch 2014's Arandic examples are drawn mainly from Central/Eastern Anmatyerr (Green 2010).

sources.note: p.55: Arandic-wide rule 'main stress falls on the first vowel that follows a consonant' = 'the second syllable with VC(C) syllables'. Secs 4.6-4.7 (pp.62-64) are first-hand notes on Eastern and Western Anmatyerr; p.63 applies the rule (initial /ye/ vs /e/ distinguished by the vowel being stressed after /y/; '/h/.. when it precedes the primary stressed vowel'). Earlier (approx. pp.50-53) notes speakers transferring stress to the initial vowel of short surface VCV words.
